COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
I.A. No. 1 of 2026
In 
CRLR No. 94 of 2026
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. B.S. Bhandari and Mr. S.S. Mehra, 
learned counsel for the revisionist.
2. The instant revision has been preferred 
against the order of conviction whereby revisionist 
has been sentenced to undergo simple 
imprisonment of two years with a fine of Rs. 
16,20,000/- for the offence punishable under 
Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. 
Statutory amount of 20% deposited at the 
appellate stage and now, the exemption 
application has been moved. 
3. Yesterday, learned counsel for the 
revisionist was directed to get instructions from 
his client. Today, on instructions, learned counsel 
for the revisionist submits that revisionist is ready 
to deposit Rs. 5,00,000/- in the Registry. 
4. Admit. 
5. Issue notice to the respondent. 
6. Steps within a week. 
7. Summon the trial court record. 
8. Exemption application is allowed subject to 
deposition of Rs. 5,00,000/- in the Registry within 
fifteen days from today. It is made clear that if the 
revisionist deposits, Rs. 5,00,000/- within the 
aforesaid period there is no need to surrender.
9. List on 09.03.2026.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 12.02.2026
SKS

Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. B.S. Koranga, learned counsel for the 
applicant.
2. Mrs. Shruti Joshi, learned counsel for the 
respondent.
3. The revisionist is present in court in compliance to 
the previous order and apprise that her father-in-law is 
in dialysis and she is facing acute financial hardship 
though she also apprised to this court that her husband is 
serving as Junior Engineer in Jal Sansthan. She also 
submits that she is also running a water plant but the 
same is not functioning.
4. Taking into consideration her personal hardship, 
this court is taking a very liberal approach in order to 
comply the previous order of this court, whereby, the 
revisionist was directed to deposit a sum of Rs. 5 lakhs/-. 
This revision is preferred against her conviction under 
section 138 of N.I. Act and the total amount is more than 
Rs. 16 lakhs and that was the reason, on the previous 
date the exemption was allowed subject to the condition 
that the revisionist shall deposit a sum of Rs. 5 lakh, but 
she failed to do so. Now, she assures this court that 
within two months she will deposit the amount in terms 
of the order dated 12.02.2026.
5. Time, as prayed for, is granted.
6. It is made clear that no further opportunity shall 
be given t comply on expiry of the aforesaid period.
7. List this matter on 17.09.2026.
8. On that day the learned counsel for the revisionist 
shall file the receipt of deposit of the aforesaid amount.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 20.08.2026
